Comment: Run Task Helper (Event-Driven) - Execute task, emit event on completion, callback to pipeline

Check_Should_Skip_Task.Comment: Skip this task if its task_name is in the skip_tasks list. Used by task_subset backfill (ADR #51) — backend computes the complement of user-supplied subset and passes it through bulk_backfill SFN → user pipeline ASL → here. Default branch preserves existing flow for normal scheduled runs.

Task_Skipped.Comment: Task was in skip_tasks list — emit synthetic 'skipped' result so downstream tasks with trigger_rule 'all_done' proceed correctly.

Check_Execution_Paused.Comment: Check if pipeline execution is paused

Catch.Comment: DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)

Route_Pause_Check.Comment: If paused, wait for callback; otherwise continue

Save_Pause_Token_And_Wait.Comment: Call pause_waiter helper and wait for Resume callback (12h timeout)

Update_Status_Running.Comment: Update DynamoDB: status = running, record running_at timestamp and run_task_helper_arn. ConditionExpression guards against a ghost (prior-attempt) execution overwriting run_task_helper_arn or resetting the attempt counter for the current attempt. Uses <= (not strict <) for idempotency: same-attempt retries on DDB throttle can safely re-write the same values.

Arguments.UpdateExpression: SET #s = :status, running_at = :running_at, run_task_helper_arn = :helper_arn, task_run_id = :task_run_id, attempt = :attempt, task_arn = :task_arn, task_type = :task_type

Catch.Comment: A newer attempt (restart) has already advanced past this attempt's status write — ghost write correctly rejected. End quietly so the current attempt's outcome is what downstream sees.
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)

Check_Has_Dependencies.Comment: If task has dependencies, read their outputs for upstream context

Get_Dep_Output.Output: {% ( $raw := $states.result.Item.result.S; $safe := $exists($raw) and $length($raw) > 25000 ? '{"_truncated":true,"_size":' & $string($length($raw)) & ',"_warning":"Output exceeded 25KB upstream limit. Full output preserved in DynamoDB. Use S3 pointers for large data."}' : $raw; $isJson := $exists($safe) and ($safe = '{}' or $safe = '[]' or $substring($safe, 0, 2) = '{"' or $substring($safe, 0, 2) = '["' or $substring($safe, 0, 2) = '[{'); $parsed := $isJson ? $parse($safe) : {'_raw': $safe}; { 'task_name': $states.input.dep, 'output': $exists($safe) ? $parsed : {}, 'status': $exists($states.result.Item.status.S) ? $states.result.Item.status.S : 'unknown' } ) %}

Catch.Comment: Read_Upstream_Outputs Map failed - continue

Prepare_Task_Input.Comment: Compute date variables (like backfill) and build final task input with upstream context

Save_Task_Input.Comment: Save task_input (upstream+variables) as soon as the task actually starts, independent of eventual success/failure/waiting_decision — Save_Canonical_Output only fires on the success path, which previously meant running/failed/manually-resolved tasks never had a recorded input to debug from. Deliberately updateItem, not putItem like Save_Canonical_Output: this key (output#pipeline#task#date) is shared across same-day runs of this task, so a blind full-item replace here could momentarily blank out a prior successful run's real 'result' while this run is still in flight. SET only touches task_input/updated_at; ttl is set only if not already present, so it isn't reset by every subsequent run.

Catch.Comment: DDB failure - continue with execution; input recording is best-effort, same pattern as every other status write in this template

Check_Task_Type.Comment: Route to appropriate runner based on task_type. Default is 'sfn' for backward compatibility.

Run_Task_SFN.Comment: Execute the actual task SFN with cross-account support

Run_Task_Glue.Comment: Execute Glue job (sync - waits for completion)

Run_Task_ECS.Comment: Execute ECS/Fargate task (sync - waits for completion)

Run_Task_Athena.Comment: Execute Athena query (sync - waits for completion)

Run_Task_EMR.Comment: Execute EMR step (sync). Step is expanded into literal fields — not an opaque '{% task_config.step %}' expression — so Step Functions' deploy-time schema validation can see the required Step.Name and Step.HadoopJarStep.Jar. Values still come from the user's emr_step (task_config.step); ADR #106 owns the runtime contract.

Run_Task_Batch.Comment: Execute AWS Batch job (sync - waits for completion)

Check_Should_Retry.Comment: Retry the task in-place while attempts remain (ADR #107); otherwise fall through to the existing failure path.

Wait_Before_Retry.Comment: Wait between retries. Base = fixed retry_delay, or exponential min(retry_delay*2^attempt, max_retry_delay) when retry_backoff. With retry_jitter, apply equal jitter: a random value in [base/2, base) (ADR #107).

Increment_Retry.Comment: Bump the attempt counter and strip the prior error before re-dispatching via Check_Task_Type.

Save_Error_Waiting.Comment: Save error and set status to waiting_decision BEFORE sending Slack - so UI shows task is awaiting human decision

Catch.Comment: A newer attempt (restart) has already progressed past this attempt's status - this write was correctly rejected. End quietly rather than telling Slack/the UI this attempt is awaiting a decision, which would be stale and misleading now that a newer attempt is in flight.
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)

Stale_Attempt_Superseded.Comment: §9: a newer attempt (restart) has already progressed past this attempt's own status write - this execution's outcome is superseded and must not report itself as finished, waiting, or failed. Ends quietly with no further side effects (no TASK_FINISHED event, no dependent notification, no Slack message) - the newer attempt's own eventual outcome is what downstream should see.

Save_Success.Comment: Update DynamoDB: status = success, save result and task_execution_arn (truncates large results)

Catch.Comment: A newer attempt (restart) has already progressed past this attempt's status - this write was correctly rejected. End quietly rather than saving canonical output / notifying dependents with an outcome that's already been superseded.
DDB failure - skip canonical, continue

Save_Canonical_Output.Comment: Save canonical output under stable key (output#pipeline#task#date) for upstream reads. Survives incremental backfill - auto-skip never overwrites this.

Catch.Comment: Canonical save failed - continue (best-effort)
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)

Notify_Dependents.Comment: Notify waiting tasks via SFN helper (sync - ensure delivery)

Retry.Comment: Retry transient Lambda errors inside notify_dependents

Catch.Comment: Notify failed after retries - fail the task (visible error)

Check_Has_Outlets.Comment: Emit asset events only if (a) task has outlets AND (b) caller did NOT set _suppress_asset_event=true. Suppression is used by cascade='none' backfills (ADR #57) to run an isolated backfill without triggering downstream consumers.

Emit_Asset_Events.Comment: Record asset events and notify consumers via SFN

Record_Asset_Event.Comment: Record asset event in DynamoDB for UI staleness and pull-based consumers

Notify_Asset_Consumers_SFN.Comment: Notify pipelines subscribed to this asset (sync - ensure delivery). Uses aws-sdk:sfn:startSyncExecution because NotifyAssetConsumersSfn is EXPRESS — startExecution.sync:2 fails silently on Express SFN per CLAUDE.md.

Catch.Comment: Asset event emission failed - fail the task

Notify_Asset_Subscribers.Comment: Notify tasks waiting for these assets (pull-based, sync)

Catch.Comment: Asset notify failed - fail the task

Check_Orchestration_Token_Success.Comment: Only send callback if orchestration_token exists

Send_Pipeline_Success.Comment: Callback to pipeline: sendTaskSuccess with orchestration_token

Catch.Comment: Token expired, invalid, or already used - continue anyway

Interactive_Slack.Comment: Send Slack notification with Skip/Restart/Fail buttons

Catch.Comment: If Slack fails, record in DDB then wait for decision (can use API/Console)

Save_Slack_Failed.Comment: Record Slack notification failure in DynamoDB so UI can show warning

Catch.Comment: If DDB update fails, still continue to wait

Wait_For_Decision.Comment: Wait for user action via Slack buttons

Save_Failed.Comment: Update DynamoDB: status = failed, save error

Catch.Comment: A newer attempt (restart) has already progressed past this attempt's status - this write was correctly rejected. End quietly rather than notifying dependents/alerting with a failure outcome that's already been superseded by a restart.
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)
DDB failure - continue with execution (status update is best-effort)

Notify_Dependents_Failed.Comment: Notify waiting tasks of failure (critical for trigger_rules like all_done)

Catch.Comment: Notify failed - still send failure callback to pipeline

Check_Orchestration_Token_Failure.Comment: Only send failure callback if orchestration_token exists

Catch.Comment: Token expired, invalid, or already used - continue to fail state

Get_Decision_Timeout.Comment: Read the global decision-wait timeout from the reserved __global_settings__ registry record (ADR #103 1b). One value for the whole deployment; the Team UI can edit it, the free tier shows it read-only. Degrades to the 18000s (5h) default on any miss so the wait always has a value.

Catch.Comment: Registry read failed - use the default timeout

Check_Is_Backfill.Comment: Skip alerting for backfill runs - but still wait for user decision via UI

Send_PagerDuty_Alert.Comment: Send PagerDuty alert immediately so on-call can act during 5h wait window. Uses aws-sdk:sfn:startSyncExecution because PagerDutyAlerterSfn is EXPRESS — startExecution.sync:2 fails silently on Express SFN per CLAUDE.md.

Catch.Comment: PagerDuty failed - continue to wait (best-effort alerting)
